panels.visual: Socrates barefoot in the snow in the same old cloak, a belly, bulging eyes, cheerful, a shivering soldier next to him
panels.caption: My friends said I looked like a satyr: snub nose, bulging eyes. I walked barefoot, even in winter.

panels.visual: Socrates as a stonemason's son with a chisel in a workshop, then as a soldier with a shield, in a split frame
panels.caption: I was a stonemason's son and I fought as a soldier for Athens.

panels.visual: The priestess at Delphi (Pythia) on a tripod in swirling mist, golden glow, saying 'no one is wiser than Socrates', Socrates' face confused
panels.caption: The oracle at Delphi said no one was wiser than me.

speech.speaker: Socrates
speech.text: I know that I know nothing.

panels.visual: Socrates cornering a pompous Athenian with a pile of question marks flying, the Athenian turning red and sweating
panels.caption: I went round asking people what courage, justice and beauty were. It made me very annoying.
